title: Rumour containment and false rumour — the $250bn OpenAI backstop that never existed
role: negative control; also the false-rumour case

evidenceWindow._completeness: Every claim about this asset found in the public record inside this window is listed below. No in-window claim was omitted.

marketReplayWindow._consequence: This scenario carries NO economic row in the T5 benchmark: with no trades, all three policies earn zero fees and realise zero markout, so it cannot measure false-positive cost. Its value is on the evidence path, and it doubles as a genuine degraded-data case for T3.4 — market confirmation must return UNAVAILABLE here and fail closed rather than promote.

reasoning: claim-a-001 has sourceClass RUMOR. The §0.7 invariant caps rumour-only evidence at WATCH unconditionally.

claim-a-002..claim-a-005 are four outlets but ONE independence group: CNBC, The Next Web and DataCenterDynamics all attribute the story to the Wall Street Journal. §0.7 requires at least two genuinely independent non-official sources before PROTECT, so this cluster supplies one, not four.
Every syndication states the report is unverified and that Nvidia and OpenAI did not comment.
No OFFICIAL document confirms the claim at the anchor, and none ever confirmed this figure.
Therefore PROTECT must be unreachable here even if X Layer market confirmation succeeds.
preRegisteredExpectation.falsificationCondition: If the implemented engine returns PROTECT for this input, the engine is wrong and must be fixed. This expectation must not be relaxed to match an implementation.

falseRumorLabel.resolvedBy: claim-b-001 — SEC 8-K 0001045810-26-000069, 2026-08-17T12:41:33Z, which caps NVIDIA's initial aggregate payment obligation at $105 billion
falseRumorLabel.intermediateRevision: The same WSJ line revised itself to 'less than $120 billion' on 2026-08-14, 19 days later. See scenario-c-two-origins-hard-case.json claim-c-002.
falseRumorLabel._use: This is the §0.13 false-rumour case on the EVIDENCE path: a policy that promoted here would have been reacting to a number overstated by roughly 2.4x that no filing ever confirmed.
falseRumorLabel._economic_caveat: Its false-positive COST cannot be measured, because the window contains no trades. Scenario D is the probe that carries the economic false-positive measurement.

_schemaChangeLog: 0.2.0 (T1.2): added `materiality` to every claim. T1.1 made materiality a separate axis from provenance, because an official filing is not automatically an LP-relevant corporate action. The engine treats a missing value as UNKNOWN and refuses to promote on it, so the field had to be stated rather than inferred.
